metadata.short_desc: Customize QQ Official bot command panel content via AstrBot WebUI
metadata.desc: Displays user-customized command entries in the QQ Official bot command panel. Users add the commands they want to show, the plugin writes them verbatim to the panel. Supports 4 scenes: private chat, group chat, text channel, channel DM.

language.hint: zh-CN=Simplified Chinese, en-US=English, ru-RU=Russian, ja-JP=Japanese. Affects logger output; user-authored selected_commands entries are NOT translated. This page is the legacy compatibility configuration; use the Robots page in the plugin view instead.

primary_color.hint: Primary accent color for the plugin view in #RRGGBB format. You can also adjust it on the Settings page of the plugin view.

secondary_color.hint: Secondary accent color for the plugin view in #RRGGBB format. You can also adjust it on the Settings page of the plugin view.

scenes.description: Active scenes (where QQ command panel is visible)
scenes.hint: c2c=Private chat, group=Group chat, channel=Text sub-channel, dm=Channel DM. channel/dm only support global configuration. This item belongs to the compatibility configuration and only applies to AppIDs not taken over on the Robots page.

qq_platforms.hint: ⚠️ Legacy compatibility configuration: the new version configures each bot separately, so prefer the Robots page in the plugin view. Once an AppID appears on the Robots page, the new version takes it over and the scenes and command entries on this page are ignored. The plugin can only read credentials from here: AstrBot does not expose platform adapter bot info to plugins, so appid + clientSecret must be filled in manually. Add multiple entries for multiple bots. ⚠️ secret is masked on this page, but still saved in plain text in the config file, so do not share the config file.

name.hint: Used only to distinguish entries in the panel, can be left empty

appid.hint: AppID in QQ Bot Dashboard -> Development Settings -> Bot Basic Info

secret.hint: Masked in the config page by default; click the eye icon to reveal it temporarily. The value is still stored in plain text in the config file, so do not share the file under data/config/

platform.hint: Default qq_official works for most cases

selected_commands.description: Custom command entries to show in the QQ command panel
selected_commands.hint: Manually add entries to display in the QQ command panel. Each {name, desc} is written verbatim, independent of commands already registered in AstrBot. Max 20 entries; name ≤ 14 chars, desc ≤ 30 chars. You can also maintain them on the Compatibility page of the plugin view. This item belongs to the compatibility configuration and only applies to AppIDs not taken over on the Robots page.

name.hint: The name users see in the QQ panel, e.g. /foo; leading / is optional

desc.hint: Max 30 chars, displayed in the QQ panel

dashboard.title: Command Panel
dashboard.description: Configure the entries written to the QQ Official bot command panel and watch the sync progress.

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: Watch plugin logs in real time. The latest 1000 entries from this process are kept in memory.

logs.noMatches: No logs match the current filters.
logs.empty: No logs yet. Waiting for plugin output.

logs.mockHint: Local dev environment: showing mock logs, not connected to the AstrBot backend.

status.title: Overview
status.subtitle: Check the current state of each QQ platform and its on-line command panel.
status.mockHint: Local dev environment: showing mock data, not connected to the AstrBot backend.
status.panelsPartial: Some scene queries failed; this value is a lower bound.

sync.title: Sync panel
sync.subtitle: Write the configured entries to the QQ panel, with live progress.
sync.disabledMock: The AstrBot backend is unavailable in local dev, so syncing is disabled.

platforms.title: No QQ platform available yet
platforms.description: Fill in appid / ClientSecret under qq_platforms on the Compatibility page, or create robots on the Robots page. The plugin cannot read bot credentials from AstrBot platform adapters, so this is the only place to configure them.

commands.description: No command entries configured; syncing would delete the panels created by this plugin. Add entries under selected_commands on the Compatibility page.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Plugin-wide general settings will live here.
settings.mockHint: Local dev environment: editable preview, saving is disabled.
settings.basicSubtitle: The log language only affects plugin logs.
settings.themeSubtitle: Adjust the plugin view primary and secondary colors. Saved colors apply to both light and dark themes immediately.
settings.aboutDescription: Maintain command entries by robot and scene, then sync them to the QQ Official bot command panel.
settings.githubDescription: Browse the source code, changelog, and issue tracker.

compatibility.title: Compatibility
compatibility.subtitle: Legacy global scenes, platform credentials and command entries stay available here. Bots taken over by a robot on the Robots page with the same AppID no longer use this configuration.
compatibility.mockHint: Local dev environment: showing mock data, saving is disabled.
compatibility.basicSubtitle: Scenes decide where the command panel is visible; this only applies to bots not taken over by a robot on the Robots page with the same AppID.
compatibility.platformsSubtitle: The plugin can only read credentials from here; bots configured in AstrBot platform adapters are not synced over. Leave ClientSecret empty to keep the current value.
compatibility.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the current value
compatibility.noPlatforms: No platform yet; add one with appid + ClientSecret.
compatibility.commandsSubtitle: At most {items} entries; name ≤ {name} chars, desc ≤ {desc} chars.
compatibility.noCommands: Without command entries, syncing deletes the panels created by this plugin.
compatibility.platformSecretRequired: ClientSecret is required for a new platform.

robots.title: Robots
robots.subtitle: Maintain per-robot command entries for each scene; each robot takes effect independently.
robots.createSubtitle: Fill in the name and platform credentials first; configure each scene's command entries after creating it.
robots.mockHint: Local dev environment: showing mock data, saving is disabled.
robots.listSubtitle: Select a robot to edit its per-scene commands.
robots.emptyRobots: No robot yet. Add one first.
robots.removedLocal: Removed from the local list. It will be written to config after saving.
robots.removedMock: Removed from the local list (preview only); nothing will be written to config.
robots.basicSubtitle: Name, AppID, and platform credentials belong only to this robot.
robots.name: Robot name
robots.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the current value
robots.secretRequired: ClientSecret is required for a new robot.
robots.secretRequiredForAppidChange: ClientSecret is required after changing the AppID.
robots.appidChangeWarning: Changing the AppID changes which compatibility robots this configuration takes over: the old AppID falls back to the compatibility configuration, and the new AppID takes over the compatibility configuration with the same AppID.
robots.secretSetNoMask: ClientSecret is saved. Leave empty to keep the current value.
robots.scenesSubtitle: Each scene keeps its own command entries; an enabled scene needs at least one.

scene.noItems: This scene has no command entries yet.
scene.disabledHint: The scene is disabled. Enable it to manage command entries.

robots.dangerText: Deleting only removes the configuration here; it does not clean up existing QQ online panels.
robots.deleteConfirmText: The change is written only after saving. Existing QQ online panels will not be removed.
robots.importSubtitle: Choose or enter legacy platform AppIDs to import, one per line or separated by commas.
robots.importEmpty: No importable AppID in the compatibility configuration; enter one manually.
robots.imported: Robots imported and saved from the compatibility configuration. Review them before syncing.
robots.notLoaded: Robot configuration is not loaded yet.
robots.sceneRequiresItem: An enabled scene needs at least one command.
robots.sceneItemsTooMany: Too many command entries in one scene.
